test_title: PYST 15: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 11 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Who was the leader of the 'Indian National Army' before Subhas Chandra Bose took charge?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohan Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mohan Singh** was an Indian military officer and a key figure in the formation of the **Indian National Army (INA)**.
 
• The INA was initially formed in 1942 in Singapore with the help of the Japanese Army, and Mohan Singh became its first leader.
 
• He envisioned the INA as a force to liberate India from British colonial rule by allying with Japan during World War II.
 
• However, due to differences with the Japanese leadership over the treatment of INA soldiers and strategic decisions, Mohan Singh disbanded the INA in late 1942.
 
• When Subhas Chandra Bose assumed leadership of the INA in 1943, he reorganized and revitalized the movement, giving it a new direction and purpose.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian National Army (INA):** The INA was formed to fight against British colonial rule and was composed mainly of Indian soldiers captured by the Japanese during World War II.
 
• **Subhas Chandra Bose:** Bose took over as the leader of the INA in 1943 and renamed it the "Azad Hind Fauj." Under his leadership, the INA adopted the slogan "Jai Hind."
 
• **Singapore Conference 1942:** The INA was first established at the Indian Independence League conference in Singapore, with Mohan Singh as its commander-in-chief.
 
• **Arzi Hukumat-e-Azad Hind:** Subhas Chandra Bose also established a provisional government of Free India (Azad Hind Government) in 1943 to support the INA's efforts.
 
• **Japan's Role:** Japan provided logistical and military support to the INA, as they sought to weaken British colonial power in Asia during World War II.
